name: Zhang
description: A star 81 parsecs away, 15 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 48356: radius 15.333 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 140.555 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.054) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 48356: effective temperature 5079 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.04)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 2.87 from 2024A&A...683A.125P; the 11 published values span log g 2.56 to 3.05, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.1% of the centre brightness

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 48356: distance 80.906 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.021), at which the luminosity and radius hold

text.card: A star 81 parsecs away, 15 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 141 times the Sun's luminosity at 5,079 K, so 15.333 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 48356: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Upsilon1 Hydrae
quotes.card: Upsilon1 Hydrae, Latinised from υ1 Hydrae formally named Zhang, is a yellow-hued star in the constellation of Hydra.
quotes.introduction: It is visible to the naked eye, having an apparent visual magnitude of 4.12.
